answer: Retrospective cluster auditing. Each identity is a vertex in a transaction graph; the system periodically scores subgraphs for anomalous co-activity, treating sudden bursts as an inlet of correlated agents. Accounts whose interaction patterns co-move beyond a threshold get flagged and throttled. Detection is after the fact, so a sybil must sustain distinct behavioral histories across many accounts to avoid the signal, raising the real cost to continuous maintenance of separate activity profiles rather than one-time registration.
